Jennifer Lawrence is reflecting on her iconic 2013 Oscars dress.
In a video interview for Allure published on Tuesday, Oct. 27, the actress, 36, looked back on some of her most memorable looks, including the Dior Couture by Raf Simons gown she wore the year she won a Best Actress Oscar for her performance in Silver Linings Playbook .
“Well, it was a wedding dress,” she said of the white strapless ensemble. “And I think I was clearly looking at dresses going, ‘More, more, more, more!’ ”
Lawrence also explained her loose bun hairstyle, saying, “You got to put your hair back if you’ve got a huge, you know, bottom. Bottom of the dress. So I’m happy we went with, like, loose back.”
The actress wasn’t so sure about her jewelry choice, however.
“I don’t know about the backwards necklace,” she remarked. “Maybe those will come back. But look at her. She’s so tired and happy.”
When sharing what advice she would give herself in hindsight, Lawrence said, “Lift up the dress when you walk up the stairs. Remember to thank the director.”
“I was too superstitious at the time to write, like, a speech because I was like, ‘If I write it down and prepare, then I won’t win,’ ” she continued. “And I think I would just tell the 22-year-old, ‘That’s not true. And you’ll regret it.’ “

Lawrence infamously tripped up the stairs as she walked onto the stage to receive her award.
During an appearance on Heather McMahan’s Absolutely Not podcast in 2020, she said she was “very sensitive” about the moment “for a very long time.”
“I was ready for it. I was very nervous and also very superstitious. I didn’t want to acknowledge the possibility that I would win. I didn’t want to write down a speech,” she recalled. “I had everything in my head. I was very, very nervous but I was ready. All of the adrenaline clears out and they call my name and I’m elated and I’m in shock. And then I fell, and it erased everything from my mind. My full brain went blank. I can look back at it now fondly but for a very long time the fall thing was very sensitive.”
Lawrence also said she was hurt when news anchor Anderson Cooper made a dig at her days later.
“Anderson Cooper, I saw him on CNN three days later saying, ‘Well she obviously faked the fall,’ and it was so devastating because it was this horrific humiliation to me,” Lawrence explained. “I don’t know if I’ll ever have a chance to give a speech like that again, so it didn’t feel good for me not to have a speech.”
